text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- Psychiatric hospitals in the Oslo area have monitored an unusual influx of teenagers seeking treatment for psychiatric problems after using amphetamines or the drug ecstasy.
- Carl I. Hagen, leader of the Progress Party, says he doen not consider himself as a candidate for prime minister in September's election.
- Against Norwegian law, building companies dump between 10 and 20 tonnes per year of carcinogenic PCBs from the renovation of old buildings.
- Only one in 10 pensioners dip into their savings, a new study shows. Among pensioners with the lowest incomes, one in four puts money aside from their pension.

- Positive half-year results at many companies lifted the Oslo bourse to a new all-time high on Thursday. Airliner Braathens SAFE and offshore supply company Aker Maritime provided the best reading for shareholders.

- Brokerage Sundal Collier & Co bought several hundred thousand shares in hardware retailers Santech Micro Group (SMG) the week before American CHS Electronics put in a bid to buy the Norwegian company. Sundal Collier is adviser to SMG in the takeover process. Jan Petter Collier, head of the brokerage, says the acquisition was an options transaction and that there was no upside for Sundal.

- Carl I. Hagen, leader of the Progress Party, says the party is ready to discuss forming a coalition government after the election in September. Hagen maintains he would prefer a Labour government compared with the so-called three-party Centre-alternative, where the Centre Party would be dominant.

- The management in drugs group Nycomed ASA is pleased with first-half profits and the strong development in all of the company's business areas. The share market joined in with Nycomed's optimism and sent the stock seven crowns higher to 168.50 crowns.

- The five largest agricultural sales organisations had revenues last year of 25 billion crowns, the same level as in 1995. The net result for the five, however, came in at a loss of 16 million crowns in 1996 compared with a profit of 62 million crowns the year before.

- Shares in Aker Martime ASA climbed 16 crowns to 135 crowns on Thursday after the offshore supply company presented better-than-expected results for the first half. Aker Martime posted pre-tax profits of 94 million crowns, almost double analysts' estimates of 48 million crowns.

- Norwegian Applied Technology (NAT) stock fell like a stone on the Oslo bourse on Thursday when the company sent out a profit warning for the first half after it lost a contract for the Aasgard gas development off mid-Norway.

- Offshore companies Procon Offshore ASA and SAFE Offshore ASA plan a billion crown merger. Procon's share price has risen 60 percent since the company was listed on the Oslo bourse on June 4 when it was spun off from Transocean Offshore ASA.
